Agent Serving Quick Start

Use this quick start when Gollek is the inference and serving engine for Wayang-Gollek, a coding-agent runtime, a low-code agent builder, or another external orchestrator. Gollek validates and serves model requests. The caller owns planning, retrieval policy, vector stores, tool execution, memory, retries, and workflow state.

1. Start From The Serving Boundary

Check that the running Gollek endpoint is exposing the expected serving contract:

gollek agent capabilities \
  --base-url http://localhost:8080 \
  --api-key community \
  --require-serving-boundary

gollek agent contract \
  --base-url http://localhost:8080 \
  --api-key community \
  --require-serving-boundary

These commands do not invoke a model. They confirm that the endpoint is acting as an inference-serving engine rather than an agent orchestrator.

2. Pick A Route Template

Start from one of the request templates below. They are intentionally small, so an application can fill in the model id, prompt, tool schemas, and RAG context from its own configuration.

Template Feature profile Use it for
Chat agent preflight chat_agent Chat Completions with system prompts, tools, and caller-selected RAG context.
Responses agent preflight responses_agent Responses API callers that prefer instructions, input, and Responses-style events.
Embedding RAG preflight embedding_rag Embedding generation for caller-owned indexing, vector search, and retrieval.
MCP tools preflight mcp_tools MCP discovery and tool schema validation without tool execution.

The template policy defaults to requested_route, which requires the selected model, surface, and feature profile to match the requested route. Use readiness_only for loose local checks and clean for CI or publishing gates. Keep top-level route fields aligned with nested request fields. If a template contains both model and request.model, they should describe the same route; gollek agent template-check, gollek agent request-validate, gollek agent readiness, and gollek agent preflight fail locally on explicit conflicts before they call Gollek. Use --model, --surface, or --feature-profile when you intentionally want to override a saved template.

3. Check The Template Locally

Check the saved template before starting Gollek or wiring it into an agent workflow:

gollek agent template-check \
  --request-file docs/tutorials/integrations/templates/chat-agent-preflight.json \
  --json

template-check is local-only: it does not call Gollek, invoke a model, execute tools, run retrieval, or own workflow state. It catches missing model ids and explicit conflicts between top-level route fields and nested request fields, plus unsupported surfaces, feature profiles, and preflight policy profiles.

4. Run Preflight Locally

Run preflight with a template before wiring the route into an agent workflow:

gollek agent preflight \
  --base-url http://localhost:8080 \
  --api-key community \
  --request-file docs/tutorials/integrations/templates/chat-agent-preflight.json \
  --preflight-policy requested_route

For CI, use the same file and make the gate stricter:

gollek agent preflight \
  --base-url http://localhost:8080 \
  --api-key community \
  --request-file docs/tutorials/integrations/templates/chat-agent-preflight.json \
  --preflight-policy clean \
  --json

clean blocks on readiness failures, route mismatch, and warnings. The JSON output includes object: "gollek.agent_preflight_result", the requested route, the selected route, route_comparison, route_mismatches, preflight_gate, and preflight_policy.

If the selected route does not match the request, inspect route_mismatches[].requested and route_mismatches[].selected. Human output prints the same detail as mismatch: model requested=... selected=..., so CI logs can show exactly what drifted.

5. Wire The Agent Runtime

After preflight passes, keep the runtime flow directional:

  1. Wayang-Gollek or the caller receives the user task.
  2. The caller selects the route template and runs preflight.
  3. If retrieval is needed, the caller asks Gollek for embeddings.
  4. The caller searches its own vector store and selects context chunks.
  5. The caller sends rag_context or retrieval_context into Gollek generation.
  6. Gollek returns text, stream events, and tool-call declarations.
  7. The caller authorizes and executes tools, records memory, and decides the next step.

Gollek should not run the tool loop or own the vector store. That separation keeps Gollek reusable as a platform and keeps Wayang-Gollek free to evolve as the agentic system engine.

6. Use The SDK Gate

Java callers can use the same route policy through the SDK:

AgentServingPreflightGate gate = client.agent().servingPreflightGate(
    AgentServingPreflightRequest.builder()
        .modelId("demo-model")
        .surface("chat")
        .featureProfile("chat_agent")
        .request(chatRequest)
        .requestOptions(trace)
        .build(),
    AgentServingPreflightPolicy.clean());

if (!gate.ready()) {
    throw new IllegalStateException("Gollek serving gate failed: "
        + gate.blockingMessages());
}

Use gate.toMetadata() for CI artifacts, dashboards, or Wayang-Gollek startup health reports.
